user_query: trass gmail with term mgm from last 1 week
generated_sql:
SELECT DISTINCT 
u.page_id,
u.title,
u.created_time,
g.sender_email,
g.subject,
g.body_snippet,
g.message_content,
u.database_name
FROM unified_content u
LEFT JOIN gmail_content g ON u.page_id = g.page_id
WHERE u.database_name IN ('trass.gmail', 'gmail')
AND u.created_time >= datetime('now', '-7 days')
AND (
    LOWER(g.subject) LIKE '%mgm%'
    OR LOWER(g.body_snippet) LIKE '%mgm%'
    OR LOWER(g.message_content) LIKE '%mgm%'
    OR LOWER(g.sender_email) LIKE '%mgm%'
    OR LOWER(g.sender_name) LIKE '%mgm%'
)
ORDER BY u.created_time DESC
LIMIT 1000;

sample_results.subject: Re: Insane tariffs and our partnership
sample_results.body_snippet: Jaysay : The following idea outlines our current thinking : Reduce the effective tariff impact on Yeeps plush toys by allocating part of the $34.99 retail price to digital game content (which is not
sample_results.message_content: Jaysay :  The following idea outlines our current thinking : Reduce the effective tariff impact on Yeeps plush toys by allocating part of the $34.99 retail price to digital game content (which is not subject to customs duty) and only declaring the plush portion of the value during import. Why This Works: • U.S. customs duties are charged on the declared value of the physical item. • Digitally delivered content (e.g., game rewards, codes, in-app bonuses) is intangible and not dutiable if invoiced separately and delivered electronically. • By splitting the declared value, we reduce the base used to calculate the 125% tariff.  By increasing the digital value, we may be able to reduce the tariff burden. Example with Math: Scenario A – Full value declared as plush: • Retail Price: $34.99 • Declared Value (Plush Only): $34.99 • Tariff Rate: 125% • Tariff Owed: $34.99 × 125% = $43.74 per unit Scenario B – Value split between plush and digital content: • Retail Price: $34.99 • Declared Plush Value: $14.99 • Digital Content Value: $20.00 (non-dutiable) • Tariff Owed: $14.99 × 125% = $18.74 per unit Tariff Savings per Unit: • $43.74 (no split) – $18.74 (value split) = $25.00 saved per unit Percentage of Tariff Reduction: ($25.00 ÷ $43.74) × 100% ≈ 57.2% savings Implementation Notes: 1. Invoice must clearly show the split: • Plush Toy: $14.99 • Digital License/Game Access: $20.00 • Total: $34.99 2. Digital content must be: • Delivered via email, app, or account (not physically included) • Sold or licensed separately, even if bundled for marketing 3. Supporting documents: • Keep a breakdown of pricing logic and value attribution • If needed, digital content can be shown to be sold separately to justify the $20 valuation Best Regards, John Chiu President | MGM Production  M: +852 5574 5767 www.mgm-ind.com

So I think there's two ways we could reply here. Option 1: we double down on the request and say listen we know that you have eaten the cost of this batch and we're grateful for that but we see these as two separate issues. Since we're both on the same page here in predicting that these tariffs won't last long, in the meantime we request that you split the cost of the additional tariffs with us. Option 2: We have a great relationship with MGM, they are likely already wary of issues from american's driving hard bargains (or impossible ones) and we want to be a good representation of an american business and keep this relationship on great terms. They already agreed to remake the batch without even the slightest hesitation. We just agree that we are hopeful that they won't last long because of the severe implications they would have for the global economy. and ask them to keep us updated on any solutions that may become available  I think that we should go with Option two. Here's my draft: Hi John and Fionn, Thank you for your replies. Noted: you are unable to provide further accomodations for the 2025-02 batch in response to the 104% tariff at this time because you're already remaking it at your own cost. We're grateful that you are remaking this to make sure we can deliver a top notch product to our customers. You are clearly doing all that you can to handle this situation. Please keep us up to date as any new strategies for mitigating these tariffs present themselves. We'll check back in regarding this as appropriate. We are also optimistic that the 104% tariff will not last due to the severe implications that it has for global trade.  Best, Koii ---------- Forwarded message ---------
